::: {#exm-kolmogorov-simple-strings}
#### Simple strings

- For $n \ge 1$, the string $x$ of $n$ zeros has $\ckolmf{x}{n} \le c$ for a constant $c$,
  since the program "print $n$ zeros" does not grow with $n$.
  Without $n$ given, the program must also describe $n$,
  and the proof of @thm-kolmogorov-upper-bound gives
  $\kolmf{x} \le 2 \log_2 n + c'$.

- The string $x = 0101\ldots01$ of length $n$, for even $n \ge 2$,
  also has $\ckolmf{x}{n} \le c$,
  since the program "print $01$ until $n$ digits are printed" does not grow with $n$.
  Half its digits are ones, as expected of $n$ fair coin flips.

- The string $x$ of the first $n$ binary digits of $\pi$ also has $\ckolmf{x}{n} \le c$:
  a fixed program computes as many digits of $\pi$ as asked.
  The digits show no obvious pattern,
  yet they are as compressible as a string of zeros.

:::
